commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

content.text:
The rewrite of `0.svg` is done, but I could not run automated checks on it. Every verification command I tried (xmllint, a Python XML parse, and a Quick Look render) was denied by the session's permission system, which has no one available to approve prompts. I checked the file by inspection instead.

**What the file was:** a single empty root element with only the namespace, no dimensions, no viewBox, and no content. It would render as nothing with no intrinsic size.

**What it is now:**

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     width="100" height="100" viewBox="0 0 100 100"
     role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc">
  <title id="title">Zero</title>
  <desc id="desc">The digit 0 drawn as a bold oval outline.</desc>
  <ellipse cx="50" cy="50" rx="24" ry="36"
           fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="12"/>
</svg>
```

**Changes made:**
- **Added a viewBox and intrinsic size** so the graphic scales cleanly and has a default size when used as an image.
- **Added accessibility metadata** with a role, title, and description so screen readers announce it as "Zero".
- **Drew the digit 0** as a bold oval outline, since the filename suggested the content and an empty SVG had nothing else to refine. The stroke sits fully inside the canvas with margins on every side.
- **Used currentColor for the stroke** so it inherits the surrounding text color when inlined in HTML and falls back to black as a standalone file.
- **Added an XML declaration and trailing newline** for standalone-file hygiene.

If you intended "0.svg" to hold something other than a zero glyph, the structural fixes stand on their own and the ellipse is the only line to swap out. To verify it yourself, open it in a browser or run this in a terminal with approval available:

```sh
xmllint --noout /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg && qlmanage -p /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg
```
